allPostsData.title: Architecture Review Before Modernization: What to Look at in a Legacy Platform
allPostsData.lead: Most modernization programmes start with a target architecture and end with a half-finished migration. A two-week architecture review turns the order around: first find out where the legacy platform slows delivery, which technical debt carries business risk and what to change first, then write the roadmap.
allPostsData.metaDescription: How a software architecture review of a legacy platform works: the four questions it answers, the two-week method of interviews, system walkthrough, CI/CD review and targeted code review, and what a prioritized 90-day modernization roadmap contains.

allPostsData.title: A Monorepo for Your Laptop: Git Submodules as a Development Workspace
allPostsData.lead: A monorepo makes cross-package work easy and couples everything else. Separate repositories keep packages independent and make local development painful. A thin workspace built from git submodules gives developers the linked, single-checkout experience while every package and app stays a complete repository that builds, tests, releases, and deploys on its own.
allPostsData.metaDescription: How to use git submodules and package-manager workspaces to assemble a local development monorepo: packages are symlinked on developer machines, while CI, builds, and production consume published semver versions from a registry.

allPostsData.title: Your Building Blocks Set the Ceiling on AI-Assisted Delivery
allPostsData.lead: AI made code generation cheap; it did nothing to reduce the cost of being wrong. Shared packages, explicit contracts, executable rules, and reliable gates now determine how much useful work a team can get from AI-assisted development.
allPostsData.metaDescription: Why shared packages, contracts, executable architecture rules, and process gates decide the quality of AI-native software development: what to extract, which rules to enforce, how to gate agent work, and why security has to move into the platform.

allPostsData.title: Designing Systems Before Coding Them
allPostsData.lead: Many teams still generate API contracts after the implementation. Designing the interface first gives backend, frontend, QA, and service consumers one artifact to review, validate, and build against before integration problems become expensive.
allPostsData.metaDescription: Spec-first development replaces guesswork with explicit contracts. By combining OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, and JSON Schema, teams can generate clients, validate payloads, improve security, and deliver faster with fewer integration failures.
